text:
ana: quick sync — we need to decide sequencing for pricing changes: tier redesign vs reserved capacity v2. customers keep asking for both. want a short RICE-backed take + launch criteria. who has time to sketch tradeoffs?

sam: high-level: reserved capacity buys revenue predictability and enterprise traction. tier revamp reduces churn and helps self-serve. prefer landing reserved as a paid add-on first.

dmitri: FYI reserved v2 is non-trivial infra-wise — needs capacity isolation, improved autoscaler, and CD for failover. timeline estimate: 8–12 wks for a secure beta + 2wks for infra hardening.

emily: from sales: reserved is what the top 10 prospects ask for. impact = high on closed ARR. tiers helps SMB expansion.

jordan: usage snapshot: 70% customers < 5qps, 20% 5–50qps, 10% >50qps. so a small set causes most tail cost. tier redesign could reduce support tickets.

ana: (sorry, that was ana) throwing 2 quick RICE sketches — can we sanity-check numbers?

ana: ```
Project: Tier redesign
Reach: 600 new/retained customers per year (R=6)
Impact: medium-high (I=5)
Confidence: 60% (C=6)
Effort: 8 wks team work (E=4)
Score = (R * I * C) / E = (6*5*6)/4 = 45

Project: Reserved v2
Reach: 80 enterprise deals/year (R=2)
Impact: very high (I=9)
Confidence: 50% (C=5)
Effort: 12 wks infra+bizdev (E=8)
Score = (2*9*5)/8 = 11.25
```

sam: those numbers feel reasonable. the RICE favors tiers for mid-term velocity. but revenue/strategic value favors reserved. we should treat this as a sequencing problem not just score.

dmitri: sequencing tradeoffs from infra POV: do tier changes first (lower risk) -> quick wins; then parallel work on reserved infra but gated by a canary plan.

emily: commercial POV: we can push a "reserved beta" to 3 strategic customers even while infra is being hardened — signed NDA + manual provisioning. that buys time and proofs.

jordan: suggestion: two-track roadmap
1) Q1: Tier redesign launch (self-serve, clearer rate limits, burst credits)
2) Q2: Reserved beta (3 customers, manual ops) + telemetry
3) Q3: Reserved GA with autoscaler & SLA

ana: launch criteria proposals — please thumbs if you agree
- Tier redesign: <5% error delta on gen endpoints, <10% change in median latency, billing migration tool tested on 10 customers
- Reserved beta: 2-week stability in production for each beta customer, documented runbook, billing reconciliation proofs
- Reserved GA: autoscale SLO met, failover tests, legal/compliance signoff

sam: also add metric: token-cost delta per customer segment (to detect regressions).

emily: pricing ask from sales: flexible terms for pilot customers (shorter MRR commits) and an upgrade path into annual reserved with discounts. ops wants clear migration path.

dmitri: practical note: we'll need a migration script to move customers from usage-based to reserved. rough snippet for the migration tool:

```
# pseudo
for customer in pilot_list:
  lock_account(customer)
  create_reserved_allocation(customer, gpus=alloc)
  migrate_quotas(customer)
  verify_billing(customer)
  unlock_account(customer)
```

Keep it simple, idempotent.

billing-bot: FYI estimate: if 10% of high-usage customers purchase reserved, ARR uplift ~ $420k (rough). (calc based on current SKU rates) :moneybag:

ana: ok actions:
- emily: pick 3 pilot accounts and confirm legal terms (ETA Tue)
- dmitri: draft canary plan + migration tool PR (ETA Fri)
- sam: add token-cost delta to launch criteria (ETA Wed)
- jordan: run churn sensitivity analysis for tier boundaries (ETA Thu)
- ana: I'll draft a short comms doc for sales + docs once we lock sequencing

ana: if no objections by EOD tomorrow we lock Q1=tiers, Q2=reserved beta. :+1:

sam: +1

emily: +1

dmitri: +1, will start infra tasks

jordan: +1

ana: thanks everyone — keeping this thread as single source of truth for decisions.
